elements.texte:
[cheerful] NutriBoost is preparing the monthly report on its orders.

For each month, management wants to know the number of shipped orders and those still being processed.

The date and status of each order are in the orders table.

To extract the month from a date, use string format time.
elements.avant: Group rows by several columns at once: one group per combination of values.
elements.apres: First try: group by status gives 2 rows.
phrases: NutriBoost is preparing the monthly report on its orders.
For each month, management wants to know the number of shipped orders and those still being processed.
The date and status of each order are in the orders table.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] First try: group by status gives 2 rows.

In total: 11 shipped orders and 5 being processed.

But there’s no way to tell July from August.

Second try: group by month gives 14 orders in July and 2 in August.

This time, it’s the statuses that are mixed up.

We need to group by the month and the status at the same time.

So we group the orders by month and by status with group by.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] Group by month, status forms a group for each combination of month and status.

Two orders go in the same group if they have the same month and the same status.

July and shipped: 11 orders.

July and processing: 3 orders.

August and processing: 2 orders.

The 16 orders form 3 groups, so 3 rows in the result.

Count star then counts the orders in each group.

elements.texte:
[cheerful] What about the orders shipped in August?

There aren’t any: this group doesn’t exist.

Group by creates no row for a combination that isn’t in the table.

So the result has no row with 0 orders.

Only groups that have rows show up in the result.
